records.name: R. J. Anderson
records.bio: The workshop delivery book names Anderson as buyer for two Queen’s College Galway orders: eighty-one models on 27 January 1886 and fifty-one on 19 January 1889. The two orders provide an unusually clean person-to-institution link for the Galway collection.
records.open: A fuller authority identification for R. J. Anderson remains to be added.

records.name: A. C. Haddon
records.roles: professor of zoology · Royal College of Science for Ireland buyer
records.bio: An original invoice dated 13 June 1885 records Haddon, Professor of Zoology at the Royal College of Science for Ireland, as buyer of 139 Blaschka models. The order is one of the strongest surviving Irish person-level acquisition records because the buyer, date, quantity and direct workshop route are all preserved.

records.name: Andrew Leith Adams
records.roles: professor · Queen’s College Cork acquisition actor
records.bio: Adams is the named university-side actor in the Cork collection history. A workshop draft records an earlier set already delivered and a later order of about 100 Reichsmarks to be prepared after the Dublin commissions, with Robert Damon involved in the later route.
records.open: No complete Cork order list survives in the recovered study, so the two order contents and total original model count remain unresolved.

records.name: Robert Oliver Cunningham
records.roles: professor of natural history · Belfast buyer
records.bio: Cunningham was identified in the Irish collection study as the Queen’s College Belfast professor whose Blaschka order was prepaid through Robert Damon for £8, or 160 Reichsmarks. A later workshop letter records dispatch of one box to him in Belfast.
records.open: The order list has not been located and the collection is currently unlocated; the backend preserves only an estimated original range of roughly forty-five to fifty-five models.

records.name: William Johnston Sollas
records.roles: geology professor · Trinity College Dublin buyer
records.bio: The Blaschka records identify ‘Professor Sollas’ of Trinity College Dublin as buyer of twenty-seven models on 29 April 1885: seventeen catalogue models and ten specially commissioned molluscan dissection models. Trinity’s institutional history identifies William Johnston Sollas as the geology chair of this period.

records.name: Dr Alexander Carte
records.roles: museum curator and director · Dublin acquisition context
records.bio: The Irish network reconstruction names Carte among the museum-side officials associated with the Royal Dublin Society Natural History Museum collection. The institution made repeated Blaschka purchases, and the modern study treats Carte as a likely acquisition actor while preserving the distinction between museum office and item-level ordering evidence.
records.open: The extent of Carte’s personal role in selecting, authorising or paying for individual Blaschka orders remains unresolved.

records.name: Professor Mackintosh
records.roles: Trinity College Dublin recipient · permanent-loan custody
records.bio: National Museum of Ireland registers record six Blaschka models sent on permanent loan to Professor Mackintosh at Trinity College Dublin on 4 November 1920. Four of those models were later reported on display in the TCD Zoological Museum, while label boards survive for two missing examples.
records.open: The backend does not yet establish Mackintosh’s full identity or exact institutional office.

records.name: Camil Heller
records.roles: zoologist · published source in Rudolf’s notebook
records.bio: Corning catalogue metadata for Rudolf Blaschka’s notebook Anmerkungen über Wirbellose Thiere III lists Heller as a contributor and records Heller’s work on Adriatic zoophytes and echinoderms at the head of the notebook. The project treats him as a scientific source embedded in workshop research rather than as a commercial actor.

records.name: Anna T. Jeanes
records.roles: patronage actor · Academy of Natural Sciences Philadelphia
records.bio: The Academy of Natural Sciences finding aid names Jeanes in the patronage history of its Blaschka cephalopod collection, and item 033 preserves her name on a damaged historical label. The project retains the Jeanes/Jeans spelling conflict exactly as documented.
records.open: The public finding aid does not yet expose an invoice, payment record or item-by-item accession concordance that separates patronage, selection and purchase.

records.name: Russell Carpenter
records.roles: Barnum Museum curator · Tufts/Corning loan actor
records.bio: Tufts archival research identifies Carpenter as the Barnum Museum curator who, in a 1965 letter, asked the Corning Museum of Glass to take Tufts’ Blaschka models on what the records called a permanent loan. That correspondence became crucial when the models were rediscovered and returned decades later.

records.name: Célestine Ousset
records.bio: The Strasbourg collection module identifies Ousset as the conservator-restorer responsible for Blaschka treatment during the 2023–2025 museum-renovation campaign. Her record links the historical 1890 collection directly to its current restoration and redisplay lifecycle.
records.open: Object-level treatment documentation remains a priority for future capture.
